subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: After glob parity is repaired, should OpenClaw allow unrelated event-loop work between sequential `agent:bootstrap` handlers as permanent runtime behavior?
rationale: The symlink regression is mechanically repairable, but the new scheduling boundary occurs while handlers mutate session bootstrap context and therefore requires runtime-owner intent.

options.title: Repair parity and approve yields
options.body: Fix explicit symlink-root traversal, then accept handler interleaving after exact-head connected-run proof shows responsiveness without context drift.

options.title: Remove handler interleaving
options.body: Keep asynchronous reads and a parity-correct yielding traversal without adding event-loop turns between hook handlers.

options.title: Narrow to asynchronous reads
options.body: Defer both custom glob traversal and hook scheduling until they have independent owner-approved proof.

recommendation.title: Repair parity and approve yields
recommendation.body: Fix explicit symlink-root traversal, then accept handler interleaving after exact-head connected-run proof shows responsiveness without context drift.

likelyOwner.reason: His merged history includes the bootstrap hook, workspace filesystem boundary, and hook-contract behavior affected by this choice.
